title: Prime Minister speaks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy
subtitle:
President Zelenskyy shares his perspective on recent developments in the ongoing conflict

PM Modi conveys India’s readiness to contribute to peaceful resolution of the conflict

The two leaders discuss ways to further strengthen India-Ukraine bilateral cooperation
date:
Posted On:
                09 NOV 2026 6:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had a telephone conversation today with H.E. Mr. Volodymyr Zelenskyy, President of Ukraine.
President Zelenskyy shared his perspective on recent developments related to the ongoing conflict.
Prime Minister reaffirmed India’s human-centric approach and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. He conveyed India’s readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at peaceful resolution of the conflict.
The two leaders also discussed measures to further strengthen India-Ukraine bilateral cooperation in various sectors for the mutual benefit of the two peoples.

title: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare actively undertakes various activities under special campaign 6
subtitle:
Campaign implemented with Nationwide Swachhata Drives, e-waste disposal, plantation and disposal of various pending matters

21st October 2026 was observed as dedicated day for DA&FW for a day-long intensive cleanliness and administrative efficiency drive across the country
date:

                09 NOV 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) has actively undertaken various activities under Special Campaign 6, implemented in two phases- the preparatory phase from 16th – 30th September and Implementation phase from 2nd October- 31st October, 2026, with a focus on institutionalizing
Swachhata
and reducing pendency in Government offices. The campaign covered disposal of pending references, public grievances, record management, freeing of office space, and segregation and proper disposal of e-waste and scrap etc. All Attached/Subordinate offices and field units of DA&FW have participated actively in the Special Campaign.
21st October 2026 was observed as a dedicated day for DA&FW
for a day-long intensive cleanliness and administrative efficiency drive across the country.
Various Activities undertaken during Special Campaign 6
1. Nationwide Plantation Drive: -
Demonstrating a strong commitment to a greener environment, various attached/subordinate/field offices of DA&FW have planted more than 2,000 plants across the country.
2. Secretary (DA&FW) Visits National Seeds Corporation (NSC):-
Secretary (DA&FW) visited the National Seeds Corporation in New Delhi to review ongoing campaign activities under Special Campaign 6
.
The visit included a plantation drive, flagging off of trucks for scrap and e-waste disposal through authorized recyclers, and felicitation of sanitation staff. The Secretary also inspected the rooftop solar power facility (84 kW capacity) and the seed processing and packing unit. Innovative initiatives such as bird feed preparation using non-seed materials, micro greens from unsold seeds, and display of value-added products were also showcased, highlighting sustainability, efficient resource utilization and the Waste to Wealth approach.
3.         Cleanliness campaigns:
The field offices of DA&FW conducted cleanliness campaigns to promote a clean and hygienic workplace. Under the Campaign, out of a target of 999 sites identified for cleanliness activities, 1179 sites have been covered.
4.         Waste to wealth models:-
Various Field offices of DA&FW including CFMTTI (Budni), MANAGE (Hyderabad), NRFMTTI (Hisar), and NERFMTTI (Biswanath Chariali)—showcased innovative models built entirely from electronic waste and discarded parts. Notable exhibits included a life-sized Rhinoceros model made from circuit boards at NERFMTTI Assam, alongside working models of sea boats and tractors crafted from scrap machinery.
5.         Review meetings:-
A number of review meetings were held during the Special Campaign 6 with the Nodal Officers of DA&FW and its attached, subordinate and field offices for smooth and effective conduct of the activities identified.
Overall Targets and Achievements made under Special Campaign 6
Driven by active field participation, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare has achieved significant milestones, in certain respects it has acceded the targets fixed. In Public Grievances, the targets of pending grievances were taken as received up to 30th September, 2026 as stipulated. However, the PG received during the period 31st October, 2026 have also been disposed off.

title: TRAI releases “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 NOV 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today released
“The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
. These amendments introduce a framework for port charges for IP-based interconnection, supplementing the existing provisions applicable to ports for E1/TDM-based interconnection. These regulations will take effect from 1st January 2027.
Interconnection in telecommunications refers to the technical, operational, and commercial arrangements that connect two or more telecom networks, allowing telecommunications traffic to flow between them and enabling users of different service providers to communicate seamlessly. Section 11(1)(b) of the TRAI Act, 1997,
inter alia
, empowers TRAI to prescribe the terms and conditions of interconnection between service providers, and to ensure technical compatibility and effective interconnection between different service providers.
The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) Regulation, 2001 prescribes the charges payable by an interconnection seeker to an interconnection provider for terminating interconnection links at its point of interconnection. The extant regulations were based on legacy E1/TDM-based port technologies, and the charges prescribed therein were last revised in 2012.
To ensure that the existing regulatory framework governing interconnection matters remains relevant, transparent, and conducive to efficient interconnection between service providers, TRAI initiated a review of the regulatory framework through a Pre-Consultation Paper on the “Review of the existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, dated 03.04.2025. Through this Pre-Consultation Paper, stakeholders’ comments were sought,
inter alia
, to review the Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) Regulation, 2001.
Subsequently, a Consultation Paper on the “Review of the existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, providing the background information and taking into account the stakeholders’ comments received during the pre-consultation process, was issued on 10.11.2025. Through the Consultation Paper, stakeholders’ comments were sought,
inter alia
, to review the Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) Regulation, 2001. After extension, the last dates for furnishing written comments and counter-comments were 15.12.2025 and 29.12.2025, respectively.
In response to the issues raised in the Consultation Paper, seventeen stakeholders submitted their comments, while nine stakeholders submitted counter-comments. As part of the consultation process, an Open House Discussion (OHD) on the Consultation Paper was held on 28.01.2026. Based on the comments received from stakeholders during the consultation process, and its own analysis, TRAI has finalised the Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026.
The salient points of the amendment regulations are given below:
Recognition of IP ports
: The definition of “Port” has been revised to include both legacy E1 ports (2.048 Mbps) and IP ports, with bandwidth expressed in Mbps or Gbps.
Ceiling on annual IP-port charges
: Annual ceilings on IP-port charges have been prescribed at ₹5.6 lakh per 1 Gbps IP port and ₹42.3 lakh per 10 Gbps IP port.
Flexibility in interconnection arrangements
: Interconnection providers and seekers may mutually agree to charges below the prescribed ceilings. They may also mutually agree to IP-port capacities other than 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps, with charges determined transparently using the same methodology as for 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps ports.
Uniformity across services
: IP-port charges apply uniformly across fixed-line, mobile, national long-distance and international long-distance services. The charges prescribed earlier shall continue to apply only to E1 ports.
Graded framework for financial disincentives
: For effective implementation of the regulations, a graded financial disincentive framework with a ceiling of ₹15 lakh per Service Area for each instance of contravention has been prescribed for contravention of specified provisions of these regulations.
The amendment regulations align the regulatory provisions with technological advancements and sectoral developments. They are expected to strengthen the interconnection framework and facilitate seamless communication across telecom networks. The regulatory framework aims to provide greater regulatory certainty to service providers while upholding the principles of effective interconnection, transparency, non-discrimination, and fair competition.
The full text of “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Port Charges) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026”, along with the Explanatory Memorandum, is available on TRAI’s website
www.trai.gov.in
.

title: Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha Arrive at Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery, Bomdila, on 8th November
subtitle: Sacred Relics Enshrined at the Monastery; Public Darshan from 8 to 13 November 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 NOV 2026 10:38AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha  arrived at Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila, Arunachal Pradesh, on 8 November 2026 and were enshrined at the monastery for public darshan. The Sacred Relics will be available for public darshan from 8 to 13 November 2026. The exposition is being organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the National Museum  New Delhi, Government of Arunachal Pradesh and the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), New Delhi.
The first day of the public exposition on 8 November witnessed an encouraging response, with around 4,000 devotees visiting the monastery to have darshan of the Sacred Relics. Buddhist monks, dignitaries, senior citizens and persons with disabilities also offered prayers and paid their respects. From 9 to 13 November 2026, devotees from Bomdila constituency and neighbouring constituencies are scheduled to visit the monastery,  to offer prayers and seek blessings.
The Sacred Relics were transported from Tawang to Bomdila aboard an Indian Air Force Chinook helicopter, accompanied by Shri Bhikkhu Khemachara, Deputy Secretary General (DSG), IBC and officials from  Ministry of culture, National Museum, New Delhi, and IBC. At the Army Helipad, Rupa, the Sacred Relics were received with due protocol by Shri Pasang Dorjee Sona, Minister for Education, Tourism, Rural Works Department (RWD) and Public Libraries, Government of Arunachal Pradesh. A Guard of Honour was presented at the helipad. Thereafter, the Sacred Relics proceeded towards Bomdila, with a brief ceremonial halt at Upper Gompa before being taken to Thubchog Gatsel Ling Monastery (Lower Gompa) for enshrinement.
Following the enshrinement, two special exhibitions were inaugurated at the monastery by the Chief Guest, Shri Pasang Dorjee Sona,  Minister for Education, Tourism and Rural Works Department, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, in the presence of Padma Shri the 12th Guru Trulku Rinpoche. The exhibitions, organised by the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC) and the National Museum, New Delhi, showcase the historical, spiritual and cultural heritage associated with Buddhism and the Sacred Relics.
The arrival of the Sacred Relics in Bomdila follows the conclusion of the seven-day public exposition at Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) on 7 November 2026. The exposition witnessed the participation of thousands of devotees and visitors from all blocks of Tawang  and neighbouring areas, who gathered to have darshan of the Sacred Relics, offer prayers and pay their respects. The overwhelming response reflected the deep spiritual reverence associated with the Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha.
Following the Bomdila exposition, the Sacred Relics will proceed to the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, where they will remain open for public darshan from 14 to 20 November 2026. Thereafter, the Sacred Relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026.

title: INDIAN NAVY TO CONDUCT PASSING OUT PARADE OF LARGEST BATCH OF AGNIVEERS AT INS CHILKA
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 NOV 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
INS Chilka, the Indian Navy’s premier ab-initio training establishment, will conduct the Passing Out Parade (POP) of the
ninth batch of Agniveers of the Indian Navy and Naviks of the Indian Coast Guard on 13 Nov 2026.
Adm Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff, will be the Chief Guest and Reviewing Officer of the Parade.
The parade will mark the successful completion of 16 weeks of ab-initio training by over 3,300 trainees, making it the largest batch to pass out from INS Chilka
. The parade will mark the culmination of an intensive training programme designed to transform young recruits into disciplined, physically agile, mentally resilient and professionally competent sea warriors.
The training curriculum integrates academics, physical conditioning, swimming, parade training, outdoor activities and camp, providing a holistic foundation for the trainees' professional journey. Equal emphasis is laid on character building, leadership, discipline, camaraderie and teamwork, while instilling the core naval values of
Duty, Honour and Courage
.
The Passing Out Parade will be a moment of pride and accomplishment for the trainees, as their families witness the culmination of training journey and beginning of a new career. Besides this, Naval veterans and distinguished guests will also be present for the occasion.
The Valedictory Function will be presided over by VAdm Sameer Saxena, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Southern Naval Command. Awards will be presented to meritorious trainees, the champion division and best instructor in recognition of their exemplary performance and contribution to training. The event will also witness the
unveiling of
‘Ankur’
, the bilingual trainees’ magazine.
The Passing Out Parade will be streamed live on the Indian Navy’s official social media platforms, enabling citizens across the country to witness the occasion.

title: INAUGURAL INDIA–MYANMAR BILATERAL TRI-SERVICES HADR EXERCISE ‘RAHAT MITRA’ CONCLUDES AT CHENNAI
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 NOV 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The inaugural bilateral Tri-Services Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Exercise
‘RAHAT MITRA’,
conducted between the Defence Forces of India and Myanmar on
05 and 06 Nov 2026,
concluded at Chennai. The two-day exercise brought together personnel from the Indian Navy, Indian Army and Indian Air Force, along with a delegation from the Myanmar Defence Forces, to enhance operational interoperability, improve coordination and facilitate the exchange of
Best Practices
in disaster response operations.
The exercise commenced with a focus on joint planning and familiarisation with HADR capabilities. A Table-Top Exercise (TTX), based on a severe cyclone scenario, facilitated discussions on coordinated response mechanisms and joint disaster management protocols. The participating contingents also witnessed demonstrations of obstacle clearance and bridge-laying capabilities by the Indian Army and visited INS Sukanya to gain insights into the Indian Navy’s shipborne HADR capabilities. (
https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2333709
)
On the second day, the participating contingents witnessed demonstrations of multi-domain HADR capabilities by the Indian Defence Forces, highlighting coordinated response mechanisms across maritime, land and air domains. INS Adyar and Communication Network Centre, Chennai, showcased shore-based disaster response arrangements and communication infrastructure supporting command and control during emergencies. Military Hospital, Chennai, demonstrated field medical triage and the coordinated management of disaster relief camps.
The Indian Navy’s Flood Relief Teams (FRT) demonstrated specialised equipment and capabilities for flood relief operations. Maritime Search and Rescue (SAR) capabilities were also showcased through coordinated manoeuvres involving a Chetak helicopter and INS Bitra. content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for various development projects worth approximately ₹1,400 crore in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Gujarat Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel and several other dignitaries were present on the occasion.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that development works worth approximately ₹1,400 crore were inaugurated and their foundation stones laid today. Of these, works worth around ₹1,024 crore have been undertaken by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC), while projects worth approximately ₹400 crore have been completed or initiated through the Gujarat Government’s Roads and Buildings Department and the Government of India.
Shri Amit Shah said that in 2007, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had launched a scheme to provide permanent houses to people living in slums, which is now being taken forward by Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel. He added that the residents of Ramapir No Tekro are now being provided with beautiful private flats. He said that once the entire project is implemented, more than 55,000 people will have access to social security, recreational, educational and healthcare facilities within a single complex. Shri Shah further said that Prime Minister Modi had launched a scheme to rehabilitate nearly one lakh slum dwellers in Ahmedabad by providing them with permanent houses, and the Chief Minister and the Gujarat Government are successfully taking this initiative forward.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that the Opposition party, which ruled the country and Gujarat from 1947 to 1995, never paid attention to areas like Ramapir No Tekro. He said that the poor continued to vote for the Opposition party for a long time, but their houses were never built. He said that the process of change began in 1995 with the election of the first councilor, and in 2012, he himself was elected as the MLA from this constituency.
Shri Amit Shah urged the residents of Ramapir Ka Tila to give priority to their children's education. Referring to the inauguration of two primary schools today, he said that the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation has transformed all the primary schools in the area into smart schools. He added that the Primary Education Committees of the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency have also converted schools into smart schools.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the foundation stone for the construction of a pump house to facilitate the drainage of rainwater in the Bopal-Ghuma area was laid today. He said that he has been associated with this area for the past 30 years and had promised that a system would be put in place before 2029 to ensure that the area never faces waterlogging. Shri Shah said that work on the four-kilometre-long ISKCON overbridge also commenced today. He said that earlier, it used to take two and a half hours to travel from Sarkhej to Gandhinagar. However, once the project is completed in three years, people will be able to cover this distance in a much shorter time through a signal-free overbridge. He added that very few cities in the world have such modern infrastructure. He further said that the Jalasapur Water Treatment Plant was also inaugurated today.
The Home Minister said that, including the projects undertaken today, development works worth ₹25,000 crore have been completed in the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency over the past seven years. He reiterated his commitment to realising the vision of a “Green Gandhinagar & Developed Gandhinagar” Lok Sabha Constituency.
Shri Amit Shah referred to the joint meeting held last Saturday between the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and the Home Department of Gujarat, during which discussions were held on the implementation of the Naveen Nyay Sanhitas (new criminal laws), modernisation of the Home Department and making Gujarat drug-free. He informed the gathering about the 1033 helpline number and said that anyone reporting the sale or consumption of drugs through 1033 would have their identity kept confidential and strict action would be taken.
The Home Minister described drug abuse as something that destroys the physical and mental health, as well as the concentration of young people, and promotes terrorism. Shri Shah said that after achieving the goal of a Naxal-free India, the Modi Government has now set a target of making a ‘Drug-Free India’ by December 31, 2029. He appealed to everyone to take responsibility for making a ‘Drug-free Gujarat’ before December 31, 2028. Shri Shah urged teachers to arrange tests and meet parents whenever they notice changes in a child's behaviour in the classroom. He also appealed to parents and citizens to fulfil their responsibility by reporting any information about drug-related activities in their neighbourhood. He said that de-addiction centres are being established for young people struggling with drug addiction. He emphasised that there should be no hesitation or shame in seeking treatment for drug addiction. He assured that the identities of such young people would also be kept confidential.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah emphasised that the fight to make Gujarat and India drug-free cannot be fought by the Government alone. The cooperation of citizens, teachers and parents is essential. He said that a control room would become operational from December 1, with a mechanism in place to ensure action within three hours of receiving any information related to drugs. Shri Shah said that a scientific mechanism has been developed for this purpose. Arrangements have also been made to ensure that the kingpins and operatives involved in the drug trade are sent to jail. Giving a guarantee on behalf of the Prime Minister and the Chief Minister, he said that the Government would not take even a single step back in its fight against the drug trade. During the programme, he also administered a pledge to local residents to actively contribute towards making Gujarat drug-free.
On the occasion, Union Home Minister also extended his greetings to the people of Gujarat on Diwali and the Gujarati New Year (Bestu Varas), which begins tomorrow.

title: President of India to Confer 10th Edition Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 Awards

date:

content:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu will confer Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 at a ceremony to be held at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi on 11th November, 2026.
The 10th edition of the Swachh Survekshan on the theme of ‘
Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel- Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath
’ has been successfully completed. Under the aegis of the Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Swachh Survekshan (SS) Awards 2025-26 will honour India’s cleanest cities, celebrating their outstanding contributions to Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban. The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, will confer awards across various categories at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, in the presence of Sh. Manohar Lal, Union Minister of MoHUA and Power and Sh. Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State, MoHUA.
The SS 2025-26 awards serve as a celebration of the collective achievements of cities and States in the past decade and a renewed commitment to sustain on-ground achievements.
Swachh Survekshan, SBM-U’s flagship cleanliness assessment, has grown in scale from 73 ULBs in 2016 to over 4,751 cities in its latest edition. Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 introduces several key enhancements, including greater emphasis on citizen feedback, expanded coverage of Urban River Fronts, Coastlines and Water bodies and focused indicators on prevention of open defection & open urination, cleanliness of tourist and heritage hotspots, and behaviour change initiatives in schools.
As part of the 10th edition of SS, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) were evaluated across
43 indicators spanning 10 key assessment areas
–
Segregation, Collection & Transportation of Waste, Solid Waste Management, Visible Cleanliness, Access to Sanitation, Mechanisation of Desludging Services, Ecosystem Strengthening & Institutional Parameters, Used Water Management, Advocacy for Swachhata, Overall Welfare of Sanitation Workers & Citizen Feedback & Grievance Redressal
. More than 3,000 trained assessors conducted extensive on-ground evaluations across the country, supported by real-time GPS-enabled monitoring. From evidence submission to verification, the assessment process remained fully digital, transparent, and subject to rigorous quality checks at every stage.
Alongside the top Swachh cities, this year’s awards also recognise top performers from the ‘Swachh Shehar Jodi’ initiative that has fostered peer learning between 70 mentor cities and 191 mentee cities across 33 States/UTs to accelerate urban waste management excellence. The ‘Swachh Shehar Jodi’ Initiative was launched by the Shri Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Union Minster, on 27th September 2025 as the first-ever urban waste management mentorship and peer-learning programme. At the launch event, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed to commence this initiative between all mentor and mentee cities.
The performance of mentee cities has witnessed significant improvement across key Swachhata indicators between
Swachh Survekshan 2024 and 2025
. Notable improvements across mentee city performances has been recorded in the latest edition of Swachh Survekshan 2025-26. In the parameter of ‘
Visible Cleanliness’ mentee cities have moved from 48% in SS 2024 to 70% in the latest edition. For ‘Door-to-Door Collection’, mentee cities were at 52% in SS 2024 and have now cumulatively reached 74%.  Mentee cities have also achieved notable improvements across key parameters such as: Source Segregation (from 16% to 30%)
,
Access to Sanitation (from 11% to 38%)
,
Used Water Management (from 32% to 53%)
, and
Advocacy for Swachhata (from 48% to 66%)
, reflecting strengthened sanitation systems and improved service delivery outcomes through dedicated mentorship from high performing cities.
Following a year of dedicated efforts, healthy competition, and steadfast commitment to Swachhata, cities across the country now eagerly await the announcement of the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 Award winners on 11 November, 2026.

The Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Through these fairs, more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamchari communities have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.
The initiative aims to promote self-employment, encourage entrepreneurship and facilitate the socio-economic empowerment of beneficiary communities.
Organised around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the two week Mela brings together India's rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship through seven distinct thematic zones. These include कला आँगन, प्रकाश चौक, पूजा पथ, सजावट बाज़ार, घराना, स्वाद चौक and मंच, offering visitors a comprehensive experience of India's artistic, cultural and culinary diversity.
A senior official in the Ministry said the Mela has witnessed encouraging sales since its commencement, reflecting the enthusiastic response of visitors and growing appreciation for products crafted by beneficiary communities.
He said the four participating corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC), have recorded cumulative sales of approximately
₹
55.46 Lakh
between November 1 and November 8, 2026.
The sales figures reflect the positive market response to the products showcased at the Mela and the growing market opportunities for participating artisans.
The Ministry facilitates the participation of beneficiaries by providing free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances and transportation facilities for their goods. These support measures help artisans overcome logistical and financial barriers while enabling them to access new markets and customers.
The Mela showcases a diverse range of handicrafts, handloom products, traditional textiles, festive decorations, lamps, home décor items and other indigenous products through more than 130 stalls.
The exhibition provides an accessible marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries to connect directly with consumers, expand their market reach and strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities.
The Mela also provides opportunities for artisans to expand their market reach through initiatives such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce platforms, and Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity and capabilities of persons with disabilities while promoting inclusion and equal opportunities.
The Mela has witnessed visits by Hon'ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar; Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale; Union Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Smt. Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya; and Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, along with other senior officials.
During their visits, the dignitaries toured the exhibition stalls, appreciated the traditional craftsmanship and interacted with participating artisans, reaffirming the Government's commitment to promoting inclusive entrepreneurship, economic empowerment and sustainable livelihood opportunities for disadvantaged communities.
A major attraction of the Mela is the series of cultural activities and programmes hosted every evening at the Manch. Artists and troupe performers from different States come together to present colourful folk dances, traditional music and regional art forms. These performances offer audiences a glimpse into India's pluralistic cultural expressions on a single platform, creating a festive atmosphere and fostering regional cultural exchange.
Citizens, families and young visitors are enthusiastically visiting the Mela to explore the diverse range of traditional products, appreciate the craftsmanship of participating artisans and support their efforts towards entrepreneurship, economic empowerment and self-reliance.
The common visitors are enjoying different colours of the Mela, and experience India's rich cultural heritage while supporting the artisans and entrepreneurs contributing to the vision of an inclusive and self-reliant India.

The encouragement and care provided by the centre also helped him rebuild his confidence, improve social relationships and reintegrate into society with dignity.
Today, Ramesh Kumar has made significant progress towards leading a stable and self-reliant life. He has started his own business, improving his economic condition and achieving financial stability compared to his earlier struggles. He is now living responsibly and has regained social respect and confidence.
Expressing gratitude for the support and guidance received from the centre, he acknowledges its important role in helping him rebuild his life.

title: National Entrepreneurship Day
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                09 NOV 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Observed on 9 November, National Entrepreneurship Day highlights the growing role of entrepreneurship in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047. With over 2.62 lakh DPIIT-recognised startups, India has emerged as the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem, creating employment and expanding opportunities for its youth. Government initiatives such as Startup India, Fund of Funds for Startups, CGSS, SISFS, Atal Innovation Mission and PMEGP support innovation, access to finance, mentorship and enterprise creation. With nearly half of recognised startups originating from Tier-II and Tier-III cities, alongside expanding rural entrepreneurship, India’s ‘Amrit Peedhi’ is increasingly transforming ideas into enterprises, strengthening livelihoods and contributing to inclusive economic growth.
National Entrepreneurship Day: Empowering Youth for Viksit Bharat
India has made significant strides in building a supportive environment for aspiring entrepreneurs. This progress holds particular significance for a nation where nearly
65% of the population is under 35
. Recognising the potential of this demographic dividend, the Government has undertaken a range of initiatives to empower young Indians across fields including entrepreneurship.
DID YOU KNOW?
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was established on 9 November 2014. The day is observed as
National Entrepreneurship Day
, reflecting the importance of entrepreneurship in India’s development journey.
Over the past decade, youth have increasingly moved beyond the role of beneficiaries to become active contributors to national development. Today, the
‘Amrit Peedhi’
is emerging as a driving force behind the vision of
Viksit Bharat @ 2047
. Entrepreneurship is central to this transformation, enabling young Indians to turn ideas into enterprises, generate employment and contribute to economic growth.
Recognising the importance of entrepreneurship in India’s development journey, the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was established on 9 November 2014. The day is observed as
National Entrepreneurship Day
.
Indicators of Growth in India’s Entrepreneurship Ecosystem
DID YOU KNOW?
The Government has recognized over 55,200 startups during FY 2025-26- the highest number of startups recognized in a single year since 2016!
The shift from job seekers to job creators reflects India’s growing entrepreneurial spirit.
India has the
3rd largest startup ecosystem
in the world.
The number has grown significantly, from
fewer than 500 in 2014 to more than
2.62 lakh
DPIIT-recognized startups as of November 2026.
Indian startups are increasin
gly launching IPOs, creating jobs, and attracting global attention.
Notably, startups are present across all States and Union Territories.
Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and Gujarat have emerged as leading regions
in terms of the number of recognized startups and direct employment generation as on 31st March 2026.
Startups have been able to create more than
25 lakh jobs (up to October 2026).
The
number of startups recognized increased by 51.6% year-on-year in FY 2025-26 compared to FY 2024-25, while direct jobs created rose by 36.1% during the same period.
Besides,
more than 1.07 lakh recognized startups have at least one woman director
or partner, accounting for ~48% of total recognized startups
(As of March 2026).
Schemes Strengthening India’s Entrepreneurship Ecosystem
Through the Government’s policy support and innovation-focused initiatives, easier access to finance, and digital platforms, entrepreneurship continues to expand across India.
The Startup India Initiative
The Startup India initiative was launched in 2016. This initiative has evolved from a policy-focused framework into a comprehensive, multi-dimensional platform that supports startups at every stage, from ideation to scaling operations. To fast-track innovation-led entrepreneurship,
several flagship schemes and digital platforms support funding, mentorship, and the scaling of startups, through the Startup India initiative.
Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS)
: The FFS is a flagship initiative of the
DPIIT
under the Startup India Action Plan, managed by the
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
. With a corpus of ₹10,000 crore, the scheme channels funding through SEBI-registered
Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
, which invest in startups. This mechanism aims to enhance access to domestic risk capital and strengthen India’s entrepreneurial ecosystem.
Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0
was notified in April 2026, with a separate corpus of ₹10,000 crore. It focuses on mobilising venture and growth capital, particularly for deep-tech, innovative manufacturing and early-growth-stage startups. Under the initiative, SIDBI has committed ₹12,623 crore to 166 AIFs, which have invested ₹28,254 crore in 1,475 startups (October 2026).
Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS):
The
CGSS
has been operational since April 2023 and facilitates collateral-free loans to eligible startups through eligible financial institutions. To boost capital mobilization, the scheme’s guarantee cover per borrower was expanded from ₹10 crore to ₹20 crore in FY 2025-26. Besides, this reduces the annual guarantee fee to 1% for 27 Champion Sectors such as aerospace and defence, bio-technology, railways, tourism and hospitality services, financial services etc. As of October 2026, the scheme has guaranteed 532 loans worth ₹1,662.71 crore to startups employing 41,637 people.
Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
: The
SISFS
, with a corpus of ₹945 crore, provides financial assistance to startups for proof of concept, prototyping, product trials, market entry and commercialisation. An
Expert Advisory Committee (EAC)
oversees the scheme’s implementation, execution and monitoring.  Under the scheme, ₹775.67 crore has been approved for 4,194 startups across 32 States/UTs through 244 incubators. This includes 2,147 women-led startups and 2,356 startups from Tier-II and Tier-III cities.
Startup India Hub
: The Startup India Online Hub (2017) is a digital platform that enables stakeholders across India’s entrepreneurial ecosystem to discover, connect and collaborate. It bridges aspiring entrepreneurs with investors, mentors and incubators while bringing together funds, academic institutions, corporates, and government bodies to foster a connected and supportive startup ecosystem.
National Mentorship Portal (MAARG)
: The Mentorship, Advisory, Assistance, Resilience and Growth (MAARG) programme facilitates easy access to mentorship for startups by connecting entrepreneurs with experienced mentors. Mentorship is intended for startups across different sectors, stages and geographical locations. It provides strategic guidance, supports business growth, and strengthens India’s entrepreneurial ecosystem.
Startup India Investor Connect Portal
: Developed in collaboration with SIDBI, the Startup India Investor Connect Portal (2023) facilitates connections between startups, venture capital funds and investors, particularly supporting early-stage ventures. It enables entrepreneurs to reach multiple investors through a single application, streamlining the process of presenting their business ideas and accessing potential funding opportunities. As of 9 November 2026, there are 11,582 startups registered on the portal.
Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)
Launched in 2016 by NITI Aayog, the AIM is the Government’s flagship initiative to foster a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship across schools, universities, research institutions, startups, and industry. AIM provides an integrated framework for developing innovation programmes, fostering partnerships, and strengthening India’s startup ecosystem. AIM 2.0, approved in November 2024, has an outlay of ₹2,750 crore up to March 2028. It expands this foundation through wider participation, stronger startup support and deeper regional collaboration.
Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)
Introduced in 2015, PMMY helps micro and small enterprises obtain loans of up to ₹20 lakh without collateral for income-generating activities in the non-corporate, non-farm sector. The Scheme offers loans under four categories based on borrowers’ funding needs and the stage of their business growth.
Loan Category
Loan Amount

Up to ₹50,000

Above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh

Above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh
Tarun Plus
Above ₹10 lakh and up to ₹20 lakh
The loans meet term-financing and working capital requirements for manufacturing, trading and service businesses, as well as agriculture-allied activities such as poultry, dairy and beekeeping.
As on
30 October 2026
, PMMY had sanctioned
2.44 crore+ loans
amounting to over
₹3.3 lakh crore
during
FY 2026-27
.
MeitY Startup Hub (MSH)
Established in 2016, the MeitY Startup Hub (MSH), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), promotes technology-led innovation and strengthens India’s startup ecosystem. It serves as a central platform connecting incubation centres, Centres of Excellence in emerging technologies, and other MeitY-supported initiatives to drive innovation and technology-led economic growth. As of 9 November 2026, MSH supports a growing ecosystem of over 6,149 startups, 518 incubators, and over 329 labs across India.
Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs (TIDE) 2.0 Scheme
The TIDE 2.0 Scheme (2019) promotes technology-driven entrepreneurship by strengthening incubators that support Information and Communication Technology (ICT) startups leveraging emerging technologies such as IoT, Artificial Intelligence (AI), blockchain, and robotics. The scheme provides holistic support across healthcare, education, agriculture, financial inclusion (including digital payments), infrastructure and transportation, and environment and clean technology. It operates through 51 incubators located in leading academic institutions and national research organisations across the country.
GENESIS (Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups)
The GENESIS (Gen-next Support for Innovative Startups) initiative aims to scale up around 1,600 technology startups, particularly in Tier-II and Tier-III cities across India. Launched in 2022, it provides funding and support to promote deep-tech innovation and strengthen emerging startup ecosystems. The initiative has a budgetary outlay of ₹490 crore for a period of five years. It seeks to strengthen India’s technology startup ecosystem through collaboration among startups, government institutions, academia and corporates.
In August 2026, GENESIS Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EIR) Cohort 3 was launched. It is a national-level programme to support aspiring entrepreneurs, innovators, researchers, students and early-stage startup founders in transforming innovative ideas into technology-driven ventures.  Notably, selected innovators can receive financial assistance of up to ₹10 lakh, along with incubation, mentorship and product-development support.
NIDHI (National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations)
Launched in 2016 by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology, NIDHI is an umbrella programme that nurtures knowledge-based and technology-driven ideas and innovations into successful startups. It builds an innovation-led entrepreneurial ecosystem that promotes socio-economic development through wealth and employment generation. NIDHI has made significant contributions to India’s startup ecosystem. It has supported over 12,000 startups, over 200 Technology Business Incubators (TBIs), generating over 1,30,000 jobs. Further, it has contributed to the creation of over 1,150 intellectual property (IP) assets (11 October 2026).
ASPIRE (A Scheme for Promotion of Innovation, Rural Industries and Entrepreneurship)
ASPIRE
promotes
innovation
and
entrepreneurship
in
rural
and
underserved areas
. It focuses on setting up Livelihood Business Incubators (LBIs) for micro-enterprise creation, skilling and re-skilling opportunities, and workforce supply to industrial clusters. As of October 2026, 109 LBIs have been approved and more than 1 lakh beneficiaries skilled.
Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
The
Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
promotes self-employment by supporting the establishment of new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector. It provides beneficiaries with a margin money subsidy linked to bank loans to help meet the cost of setting up these enterprises.
The scheme is implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) under the Ministry of MSME, ensuring wider outreach and effective last-mile delivery.
Project Cost Limits:
The scheme supports projects with costs of up to ₹50 lakh in the manufacturing sector and ₹20 lakh in the service sector.
The scheme provides assistance under General and Special categories. The Special Category covers SC/ST/OBC communities, Minorities, Women, Ex-servicemen, Persons with Disabilities and Transgender applicants, as well as beneficiaries from the Northeastern Region, Hill and Border areas, and Aspirational Districts.

PM
Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)
Launched in June 2020, the
Prime Minister Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)
is a micro-credit scheme for street vendors.
Loans and credit facilities:
It supports vendors’ working capital needs through collateral-free loans that increase from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 and then ₹50,000, backed by interest subsidies and credit guarantees. Those who repay the second loan can also qualify for a UPI-linked RuPay credit card with a ₹30,000 limit.
Digital participation:
Vendors receive up to ₹1,600 in cashback for retail and wholesale digital transactions.
Welfare coverage:
Under
SVANidhi se Samriddhi
, access to eight selected Central welfare schemes is facilitated for vendors and their families on the basis of socio-economic profiling.
As of 9 November 2026, the scheme had reached over
80.7 lakh beneficiaries
, with more than
₹20,400 crore sanctioned.
Swavalambini Scheme
This scheme, launched in 2025, supports young women from business ideation to enterprise creation through entrepreneurship training, financial and market guidance, and legal support. Selected participants receive 21 weeks of mentorship and handholding to help develop sustainable enterprises. Notably, targets under the Swavalambini pilot have been achieved.
Entrepreneurship Beyond Metros: Tier II, Tier III and Rural India
India’s entrepreneurial ecosystem is expanding beyond traditional metropolitan hubs.
52% of recognised startups originate from non-metro cities
, reflecting the growing geographical spread of innovation. Businesses are increasingly choosing Tier-II and Tier-III cities for their lower costs, skilled talent, stronger industrial clusters, and improving infrastructure. As innovation spreads across Bharat, emerging cities are powering the next wave of entrepreneurship and economic growth. Rural entrepreneurship is also gaining momentum through targeted livelihood and enterprise-development programmes.
In August 2026, the Government launched the
National Campaign on Entrepreneurship-II
under the
Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), for another three months, till 21 November 2026. The campaign aims to strengthen rural women’s entrepreneurship and contribute to the vision of making 6 crore Lakhpati Didis.
The Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP)
aims to promote rural entrepreneurship by enabling households to set up and scale local enterprises. By June 2026, SVEP had supported 4.32 lakh rural enterprises across the country. The programme has strongly focused on social inclusion and equitable access to entrepreneurship opportunities. Around 86% of entrepreneurs belong to SC, ST, Minority, and OBC communities.
Together, these initiatives are strengthening local enterprise creation, widening livelihood opportunities and enabling entrepreneurship to contribute to more geographically inclusive growth.
Powering India’s Journey Towards Viksit Bharat 2047
India’s startup ecosystem is transitioning from rapid expansion towards sustainable growth and deeper integration with the real economy. As the country progresses towards a projected $7.3 trillion economy by 2030 and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, startups will continue to play a significant role in driving innovation, generating employment and strengthening economic growth. Their expanding contribution reflects India’s growing entrepreneurial capacity and the potential of innovation-led enterprises to support long-term, inclusive development.

85 Pharmaceutical Companies
have reported revised MRPs for
1,364 anti-cancer formulations
,
covering 121 drugs.
With
679 brands
reporting price reductions of
more than 50%
. The highest reported reduction in MRP is
96.45%.
As a result of the price reductions the estimated annual savings to consumers is expected to be
₹3,540.38 crore
.
Consumers can check the revised MRP printed on the medicine pack and verify medicine prices through the
Pharma Sahi Daam
mobile app or
NPPA website
(
nppa.gov.in
). No chemist or hospital pharmacy can charge more than the revised MRP. In case of overcharging or any other pricing-related complaint, consumers can register their grievance through the
Pharma Jan Samadhan portal
or contact the NPPA helpline at
1800-111-255.
